newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar backs off highs but stays firm.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar backs off highs but stays firm.

text.p: White sugar futures backed off their earlier highs in modest Thursday volume but business was mostly routine with light premium selling against New York's May contract about the only feature of interest, traders said.
The spot December contract touched a high of $327.00 earlier in the session but steady scale-up selling capped the gains and values drifted lower.
"It's pretty dead -- there's been some premium selling, nothing spectacular," one trader said.
He added that May/May had attracted sellers at $81, roughly the same value as the other nearby arbitrages.
At 1616 GMT December stood $1.90 higher at $326.00 and March up $1.20 at $322.10. Volume totalled 1,293 lots.
Confusion was evident in the market over whether Sri Lanka had bought 12,500 tonnes of lesser-quality white sugar at its recent tender or decided to reinvite bids for later this week.
London traders said the country's state buying arm, the Co-operative Wholesale Establishment (CWE), bought the sugar at $343.00 a tonne c & f from a European trading house.
But traders in Colombo said the CWE had asked suppliers to resubmit bids before Friday.

Syria bought 26,000 tonnes of sugar for November shipment dates, taking 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar from a European trade house at $312.94 per tonne and 13,000 tonnes of whites at around $364 a tonne from a London-based house, market sources said. The Paris market was also slightly firmer, with December up $2.00 at $326.00 and March up $1.00 at $322.50.
